items.q: Fill up: Afferent arteriolar dilatation in the hemodynamics list is mediated by ______.
items.exp: Afferent arteriolar dilatation (mediated by prostaglandins). (Book p739)

items.q: Fill up: Efferent arteriolar constriction in the hemodynamics list is mediated by ______.
items.exp: Efferent arteriolar constriction (mediated by angiotensin II). (Book p739)

items.q: Match each arteriolar resistance change with its renal-blood-flow and net-ultrafiltration-pressure pair — 1) Increased afferent 2) Decreased afferent 3) Increased efferent 4) Decreased efferent … A) RBF ↑, NUP ↑ (favourable for kidney) B) RBF ↓, NUP ↓ (unfavourable) C) RBF ↓, NUP ↑ (unfavourable) D) RBF ↑, NUP ↓ (unfavourable)
items.exp: Table: increased afferent ↓↓; decreased afferent ↑↑ (favourable); increased efferent ↓↑; decreased efferent ↑↓ — all but decreased afferent are unfavourable. (Book p739)

items.q: Efferent arteriolar constriction reduces blood flow to the medulla and causes:
items.exp: Efferent arteriolar constriction → ↓ blood flow to medulla → medullary hypoxia. (Book p739)

items.q: In the normal-blood-flow note, the sequence after the efferent arteriole is:
opts: Peritubular capillary → renal pelvis → vasa recta
Glomerular capillary → vasa recta → peritubular capillary
Peritubular capillary → vasa recta → renal medulla
Vasa recta → peritubular capillary → renal cortex
items.exp: Efferent arteriole → peritubular capillary → vasa recta → renal medulla. (Book p739)

items.q: Which of the following statements about ACE inhibitors is TRUE per the book?
opts: Blocking angiotensin II dilates the efferent arteriole, lowering GFR (↑S.Cr) but raising blood flow
ACE inhibitors constrict the efferent arteriole
ACE inhibitors raise GFR by dilating the afferent arteriole
ACE inhibitors are harmful in all nephrology patients
items.exp: ACE inhibitor: block angiotensin II → efferent arteriolar dilatation → ↓ GFR (↑S.Cr) but ↑ blood flow; beneficial for nephrology patients. (Book p739)

items.q: A patient with bilateral renal artery stenosis is started on an ACE inhibitor and deteriorates. The book's explanation is that:
opts: Prostaglandins were blocking the afferent arteriole
The afferent arteriole is not working and the efferent arteriole was maintaining GFR
The efferent arteriole was already fully dilated
items.exp: C/I in patients with b/l renal artery stenosis: afferent arteriole not working, efferent arteriole maintains GFR — removing angiotensin II collapses that support. (Book p739)

items.q: Fill up: NSAIDs block prostaglandins and thereby block ______ arteriolar dilatation, leaving efferent constriction to lower GFR and RBF.
items.exp: NSAID: block prostaglandins → block afferent arteriolar dilatation → efferent arteriolar constriction → ↓ GFR & ↓ RBF. (Book p739)

items.q: NSAIDs are contraindicated in patients already on ACE inhibitors because blocking angiotensin II removes efferent constriction and precipitates:
items.exp: C/I in patients on ACE(−): ACEI → efferent arteriolar constriction blocked → frank renal failure. (Book p739)

items.q: All of the following are listed arteriolar events in the glomerular-hemodynamics section EXCEPT:
opts: Efferent arteriolar constriction mediated by angiotensin II
Afferent arteriolar constriction mediated by angiotensin II
Afferent arteriolar dilatation mediated by prostaglandins
items.exp: The book pairs afferent dilatation with prostaglandins and efferent constriction with angiotensin II; afferent constriction carries no angiotensin-II label. (Book p739)
